subject: hydra
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: five-headed hydra.
Style: God of War.

spec.name: Hydra of the Broken Mere
spec.description: A colossal five-headed Norse swamp hydra in a gritty, grim God of War style: scarred dark-green hide, bone and iron war-trophies, glowing blue runes, ember wounds and frost.
spec.layout: A squat, heavy four-legged reptilian beast, 9.9 m long, standing on y=0 and facing +Z. The torso is a low barrel (y 1.4–3.2, z -2.7 to 2.3) with a broad, armoured shoulder hump at z≈1.2. Five thick serpent necks root on that hump and fan out and up in a spread bouquet. Each neck rises, then arches forward, and ends in a head that dips slightly. The centre head (Mid) is the hero: tallest and biggest, head top at y≈5.8, horns to 6.2, snout tip z≈4.7. Inner heads LA (+X) and RA (-X) are about 80% scale at y≈4.6, x=±1.65, snout z≈4.5. Outer heads LB (+X) and RB (-X) are about 70% scale, lower at y≈3.8, flaring wide at x=±2.9, snout z≈4.0. A tail trails back and down to a bone-spiked club at z≈-5.2. Front legs are thick, elbows out and forward. Hind legs are digitigrade, hocks back. Each foot has 3 big claws and 1 dew-claw. The tail and legs are the only parts on the floor. A readable silhouette has a low heavy mass in the back, a fan of five necks and a clear gap between the heads. Palette use: the top of everything is darker green-grey (hideDark, hideMid) with moss on upward faces. Throats and bellies are pale bone-beige (belly, bellyShade), and mud (mud) sits at feet, belly edge and tail tip. Style (God of War 2018): desaturated, heavy, brutal and mythic. Chunky blocky scale plates are layered into overlapping armour rows, with torn flesh and old scars as pale (scarPale) thin sweeps. Hand-carved Nordic runes glow (runeBlue) on horns, bone bands and the back. Iron shackles and broken chain links hang from the body. Broken weapons (the Leviathan-style frost axe, spear shafts, arrows) are embedded in the hide. Orange ember (ember, emberGlow) glows in wounds, mouths and eyes, and frost blue (frost) rimes one head. Every head has its own identity (see parts). All details are small separate parts in their own flat colours seated on the surface, with a dark outline, then the main colour, then a fine highlight. Rest pose: all five heads face forward, jaws slightly parted and each lower jaw a separate part, necks spread, legs apart, tail straight back with a slight droop.

parts.builds: Torso, shoulders and all body armour and trophies; no legs, tail or neck tubes. (1) A low barrel torso loft from the pelvis to the chest (half width 1.4 at the hips, 1.6 at the ribs, 1.7 at the shoulders, y 1.4–3.2). It is countershaded: hideDark/hideMid on top and sides with moss patches on upward faces, belly pale on the underside, and mud on the lower flanks. (2) A broad shoulder hump (x ±1.8, up to y 3.4, z 0.3–2.2) with a ring of overlapping chunky scale plates (hideLight, hideMid) around each of the five neck-base mounts (neckBaseMid/LA/LB/RA/RB) so the necks grow out of collars; each neck base also gets a bone ring. (3) Hip and tail-root fairing so the tail tube starts cleanly at tailRoot. (4) A dorsal ridge of large overlapping bone-and-horn plates (bone, horn, boneDark) from the shoulder hump back to the tail root, each plate bigger at the shoulders, with rune-blue glyphs on the biggest ones. (5) Belly: 10–12 wide pale plates (belly, bellyShade) in a row, with a few cracked and stained with mud. (6) Visible rib bones (bone) poking through torn flank wounds (wound, blood, ember glow cracks) on both sides. (7) A Leviathan-style frost axe (iron blade with rune-blue glow and frost-coloured blade rim, leather-wrapped haft) buried deep in the left flank, with frost crystals around the entry. (8) Two or three broken spear shafts (leather, boneDark) and arrows on the right shoulder and back with iron heads. (9) A heavy iron chain (iron, ironLight links) wrapped diagonally around the barrel, with a bronze shackle ring and a snapped end dangling and a bronze Nordic knotwork medallion. (10) Long pale scars (scarPale thin sweeps) across the flanks. (11) Glowing rune circles (runeBlue) on both flanks. Everything is built from low-poly primitives with visible facets.
parts.attaches: Legs plug into hipFL/FR/HL/HR mounts, which sit inside the torso. The tail starts at tailRoot and the necks start at the five neckBase mounts, with collars covering the seams. Rides joints pelvis and chest.

parts.builds: All four legs and the tail; this part rests on the floor. Front legs are thick and muscular (shoulder bulge, upper arm, elbow plate, forearm, wide foot). Hind legs are digitigrade with a big thigh, a hock spur and a long metatarsus. Each is a smooth sweep along its hip/knee/ankle/foot joint chain, skinned to those joints, in hideDark/hideMid with a paler inner side. Layer armour on top: overlapping knee and elbow plates (horn, bone), scale rows down the shins (hideLight), and mud (mud) caked on the lower leg and feet. Each foot has 3 thick curved claws (claw colour is bone/hornTip) and a dew-claw, plus a wide pad (hideDark) with the toes spread. One front leg (footFL) wears a rusted iron shackle with a snapped chain stub; one hind leg carries a deep wound (wound, blood, ember cracks). The tail runs tail1 to tail5 as a tapered smooth sweep (radius 0.55 at the root to 0.22 at the tip; hideDark top, belly underside, rune-blue glow marks), with a dorsal row of bone plates that shrink toward the tip. At tail5 is a bone-spiked war-club (a swollen bone knob with 8–10 spikes of bone/hornTip, iron bands, and a broken harpoon head stuck in it). The feet have the lowest points on y=0.
parts.attaches: Legs begin inside the torso at the hipFL/FR/HL/HR mounts; the tail begins inside the torso at tailRoot. Feet land at y=0. Rides the leg and tail joints.

parts.builds: The centre hero head and its neck. The neck is a smooth sweep through neckMid1 to neckMid3 to headMid (radius 0.55 at the base to 0.34 at the head), hideMid on top with a pale belly strip (belly) on the front, and a row of triangular bone fins (bone/horn) down its back. Overlapping neck scale rows and 3 bronze-and-bone rune bands (runeBlue glyphs) are wrapped around it. The head is a big, 1.9 m long, wedge-shaped dragon skull (head scale constant H=1.0). The upper jaw is a separate part: a blocky snout with nostril pits (eyeDark, with ember glow inside), brow ridges, cheek plates and layered scales. The lower jaw is a separate part riding jawMid, left parted about 12°, with a chin plate, gum (wound) lining and teeth. Big readable eyes: ember-orange (ember with an emberGlow highlight and eyeDark slit pupil, dark outline ring, heavy bone brow above), under the brow ridge and facing forward. Teeth: 12–14 fangs in each jaw (tooth), long canines. A mane of 6–8 big curving antler-horns (horn at the root to hornTip) swept back from the skull crown, the two longest with rune bands and the left one snapped off, plus a frill of 5 bone spikes behind each cheek. Details: a pale scar across the snout, a bronze ring through the lower lip with a short broken chain, and ember glow in the throat. This head is the most elaborate and its colours stay dark-green with bone horns. Everything is bold, blocky and faceted.
parts.attaches: The neck starts inside the shoulder hump collar at neckBaseMid. The head joint is headMid at the back of the skull; the lower jaw hinges at jawMid. Rides neckMid1-3, headMid and jawMid.

parts.builds: Two necks and heads on the creature's left (+X): inner head LA and outer head LB. Each neck is a smooth sweep through its neck joints (radius 0.45 at the base to 0.28 at the head; LB radius 0.4 to 0.26), hideMid/hideDark on top, pale belly strip on the front, a row of bone fins on the back, and 2 rune bands in bone and bronze. Each head is a wedge skull with a separate upper jaw part and a separate lower jaw part (riding jawLA / jawLB, parted about 10°), teeth, gum, nostrils, brow ridges and big eyes. LA (scale H=0.8, 1.5 m long) is the scarred veteran: its left eye (+X side) is slashed shut by a long pale scar with stitch marks (scarPale, eyeDark), the other eye glows ember-orange, one horn is broken off at a jagged stump, the other horn carries rune-blue glyphs, and it has a jagged ear-frill of 4 bone spikes behind each cheek. LB (scale H=0.7, 1.35 m long) is the shackled one: an iron muzzle bridle (iron bands with ironLight rivets and leather straps) wraps the snout with a snapped chain trailing from the cheek ring and a short rusted spike, pale yellow-orange eyes (emberGlow) with eyeDark slit pupils, short curved horns (horn to hornTip), and moss on the top of the skull. Details: ember glow in the mouths, a pale scar on each neck, and teeth in both jaws. Colours come from the palette.
parts.attaches: Necks start inside the shoulder collar at neckBaseLA (0.8, 3.0, 1.2) and neckBaseLB (1.4, 2.9, 1.0). The heads sit at headLA and headLB. Rides neckLA1-3, headLA, jawLA, neckLB1-3, headLB, jawLB.

parts.builds: Two necks and heads on the creature's right (-X): inner head RA and outer head RB, built as the mirror in position of the left side, with the same neck construction rules (smooth sweep, radius 0.45 to 0.28 for RA and 0.4 to 0.26 for RB, pale belly strip, back fins, 2 rune bands, separate upper and lower jaw parts riding jawRA / jawRB parted about 10°, teeth, gum, nostrils, brow ridges, big eyes). RA (scale H=0.8, 1.5 m long) is the frost-bitten head: its skull and neck top are rimed with frost (frost) in angular ice crystals and icicles hanging from the jaw and horns, pale icy eyes (frost with a runeBlue glow ring and an eyeDark slit pupil), long swept horns (horn to hornTip) with rune-blue glyphs, and a breath of frost crystals at the nostrils; its hide is slightly bluer (hideLight). RB (scale H=0.7, 1.35 m long) is the burnt, ember-cracked head: charred dark hide (hideDark, wound) with glowing ember cracks (ember, emberGlow) running over the skull and snout, exposed bone (bone, boneDark) on the cheek where scales were burned off, ember-orange eyes, a mouth full of glowing emberGlow embers behind its teeth, and short split horns with charred tips. An arrow or spear (leather and iron) sticks out of RB's neck. Colours come from the palette.
parts.attaches: Necks start inside the shoulder collar at neckBaseRA (-0.8, 3.0, 1.2) and neckBaseRB (-1.4, 2.9, 1.0). The heads sit at headRA and headRB. Rides neckRA1-3, headRA, jawRA, neckRB1-3, headRB, jawRB.

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching the design for a God of War-style five-headed hydra, drawing on the game's Norse aesthetic—runes, leather, bronze/iron bindings, frost-blue and ember-red accents—and roughing out its scale with a width around 7, height 6, and length 9 units.

I'm breaking the creature into balanced parts: a torso/body section with spine ridges, chains, and scars; a legs-and-tail section with four clawed limbs and a bone-blade tail, both grounded to the floor; and then the five necks and heads split into three groups—two left heads, two right heads, and one larger central "hero" head with richer detail like a broken horn and glowing frost eyes—trying to keep the part budgets roughly even across the left and right groupings.

I'm now sketching out the actual skeleton coordinates—placing the torso roughly from z=-1.5 to z=2.0, setting leg hip and shoulder positions, extending the tail backward to about z=-5, and spreading the heads forward with the outer ones offset around x=±2.6, working out an overall bounding size for the whole creature.

Next I'm plotting where each neck rises from the shoulder mound, defining the base joints across the hump, and placing individual head positions and orientations—tallest for the center head, offset and angled for the inner left head, continuing to work outward through the rest of the heads.

I'm now mapping out the skeleton structure: setting the overall body width and size, then defining the joint hierarchy starting from pelvis and chest, and building out each neck's chain of joints toward its head and jaw.

Each leg gets four joints (hip, knee, ankle, foot), totaling 16 across all limbs, plus a five-segment tail, five necks with five joints each, and the two spine joints, bringing the total to 48 joints I need to keep consistent with how the builders will reference them.

Now I'm sketching actual 3D coordinates for the torso and legs, placing the pelvis and chest joints, then working out the front leg hip and knee positions for a sprawling reptilian stance with elbows splayed outward.

Still placing leg joints...

Continuing up the center neck chain, the curve arcs upward and forward before the head dips down to meet it, with the skull box positioned roughly from the base of the neck to the snout tip, and the jaw hinge set near the back-lower part of the head joint.

Now I'm working out naming for the side neck chains -- using Mid for center, LA/LB for left inner and outer, RA/RB for right, with matching joint names for neck, head, and jaw segments on each side. I'm placing the first joint of the left inner chain near the neck base, angled upward and forward, and continuing up through subsequent joints toward the head.

Still writing joint coordinates...

I'm mirroring the left-side joints to create the right side by negating the x-values, then adding the central neck chain running straight up the midline before noting head sizing for the middle head.

Setting head lengths relative to each limb, I'm computing the maximum z-extent to figure overall bounding box size, landing on roughly 7x6.3x9.9 for the whole figure, then sketching bounding boxes for each head segment to check for overlaps with the central body box.

I'm nudging the box boundaries since the mid and side heads' necks naturally overlap at their shoulder mounts, deciding that's acceptable since boxes are just rough guides. Now I'm moving on to the torso, planning belly plates and spine details.

For the body, I want dorsal ridge plates running from neck to tail, a shoulder hump where the neck roots meet collars at the mounts, glowing runes, and God of War-inspired elements like chains with old Norse shackles, broken weapons embedded in the hide, scars, and remnants of bone armor, plus ember cracks and frost for texture. I'm settling on a dark desaturated slate-green scale palette with a pale bone belly, cyan GoW-style rune glow, and red embers from wounds, and I'm starting to define the specific hex colors for the hide tones.

Still defining the color palette...

Now I'm planning the part budgets, allocating 170 to the body with torso loft, belly plates, embedded weapons, rune patches, scars and wounds, plus moss and mud detailing, then another 170 to the limbs and tail with clawed feet, shackles, and scale plating.

For the three heads (mid, left, right, each 170 budget), I'm giving each distinct features—the mid head gets a bone antler crown with glowing orange eyes and rune-carved horn bands, while the left head gets a scarred-shut eye with stitching and a broken horn, differentiating each head's damage and ornamentation.

I'm also planning the muzzle variants (iron bridle with chain, frost-covered icy head, burnt ember-cracked skull with fire glow) and mapping out mount points for the shoulder hump, neck bases, and tail root relative to the torso's radius so each neck attaches correctly along the body.

I'm merging the leg geometry with the tail into a single bounding box, overlapping into the torso since legs tuck underneath, with the floor plane only applying to legs not the belly. I still need to widen the head's x-extent to account for the horns.

Now I'm settling overall size at 7.0 by 6.3 and moving on to writing the full layout and style conventions: neck cross-section radii tapering from base to head, pale belly-colored underside sectors, a dorsal fin row, and head-joint geometry rules for skull, snout, and jaw hinge. I'm defining per-head scale proportions (mid vs. left/right A/B heads) and setting the left/right mirroring convention before writing out the JSON structure for parts and joints.

I'm planning a compact module that sweeps a curved path along existing named joints using a catmull spline and bone-weighted radius, keeping the implementation efficient.

I'm now working out the neck path coordinates for the right side and sketching how to build the head geometry — placing a skull frustum running forward from the head joint toward the snout tip, using scaled offsets relative to the head origin to keep proportions consistent at the given head scale.

For the head's components, I'm calculating tapered box shapes for the upper jaw and cranium, placing brow ridges above eye sockets, and figuring out eye positions by tracking how the skull's width narrows from back to front so the eyes sit correctly on the tapered surface.

Now I'm positioning the lower jaw using the relative joint offset from the head origin, building its frustum shape, and setting up teeth as rotated cones along the jaw edges—flipping upper teeth to point downward and keeping lower teeth pointing upward.

Still defining horn geometry...

Now I'm working on the neck: adding a belly strip sector along the ventral side, spike fins swept along the top of the neck, and figuring out how to place rings or bands around the neck shape.

Simpler approach: using torus geometry oriented along the tangent direction at each point of the neck sweep to form bands, plus a small glowing rune glyph box attached to one of the bands. I'm also setting the radius taper for the neck and considering how the joint path should extend through the head.

For a spike protruding from the neck, I'm sampling a frame on the neck surface and sticking a cylinder shaft embedded partway into the surface along the normal, with an iron cone tip at the end -- though I'm still working out how the embed fraction interacts with centered geometry to position it correctly.

Writing geometry code...

For eyes, I'm planning a sphere colored base with a dark slit pupil shape placed on the front, positioned using offset coordinates in the frame.

Still writing eye and nostril placement...

Now I'm defining a generic head-building function that uses the hinge joint positions as anchors, scaling offsets by head size to construct the cranium as a tapered frustum box and continuing into the snout shape.

The jaws roughly touch or slightly overlap near the hinge, so I should pose them parted by about 10 degrees after building the geometry, rotating the lower jaw joint forward to create the gap specified for the open mouth look.

Now I'm placing the upper teeth, spacing seven per side along the jaw curve and tapering their width and height to match the narrowing snout profile toward the tip.

Next I'm positioning cone-shaped teeth with longer canines, mirroring lower teeth from the jaw base upward, then adding thin gum boxes along the inside of the jaw and ember glow spheres in the throat for the red-boned variant, before shaping brow ridge boxes above the eyes.

I'm also adding cheek armor plates, a row of small scale plates along the snout top, and a chin plate beneath the lower jaw, planning to write a separate custom horn function per head type and a reusable neck-building function that takes a path and radii, while confirming the left/right eye mirroring logic across the head's symmetry axis.

For the frost head variant, I'm scattering icy crystal cones across the skull and neck, adding hanging icicles under the jaw and tiny breath crystals near the nostrils, plus a pale scar sweep along the neck using a thin lifted line segment.

For the ember-cracked head, I'm placing thin rotated boxes along the top of the cranium to act as glowing cracks, layering dark wound patches beneath them, and adding an exposed bone patch on the cheek with a darker bone-colored box underneath.

Now I'm positioning cheek bone plates asymmetrically, only on one side, sizing them to match the cranium's width taper at that height. For the split horns, I'm adding two cones per side with different directions and radii, giving one tip a charred color to suggest damage.

Placing glyph boxes along the sweep path using a sampled point, then working out the neck's curve from the spine joints through to the head, offsetting the starting point so it tucks inside the collar.

Setting radii from neck down to head to match the cranium width, then adding a belly-colored sector band and bronze/bone rune torii at two points along the neck using the sweep's local radius and tangent direction...

Still writing fin logic...

I'm deciding the palette: RA gets hideLight for the head and hideMid for the neck, while RB uses hideDark head with hideMid neck to keep the charred look. I'll bring in glow for eye highlights and sweep parts, then start writing the actual part code, estimating roughly 90 parts per head.

Now I'm budgeting the part counts carefully to stay near the 170-per-part limit, breaking down teeth, horns, frills, scales, and glyphs per head and neck combo to make sure both heads fit within the total budget.

Writing head geometry function...

Still working out the neck curve and arrow placement...

Still writing geometry helpers...
